title: Sign cookies as JSON instead of pickle
description: Signed cookies no longer use pickle. `response.set_cookie(name, value, secret=...)` now stores any JSON serializable value, signed with an HMAC (`digestmod`, default SHA-256) over the cookie name and the payload, so a signed value is only valid under the name it was set with. `secret` may be a list of secrets for key rotation: the first one signs, and `request.get_cookie()` accepts a signature made with any of them. When `max_age` (seconds or a timedelta) or `expires` is set, the expiry time is signed into the cookie as well, and `get_cookie()` returns the default once it has passed, even if the browser still sends the cookie. Given a secret, `get_cookie()` never raises and returns the default for anything that is not a valid signed cookie: a missing, unsigned, tampered, expired or old pickle-format cookie. Updates the signed cookie tests.

defects.summary: The signature does not cover the cookie name, so a value signed for one cookie is accepted under any other cookie name.
With a list of secrets the cookie is signed with the last one instead of the first, so readers that only know the current secret reject it.
The payload is decoded before the signature is checked, so a forged cookie whose payload is valid JSON of another shape raises TypeError instead of giving the default.
With a secret, a cookie that is not in the signed format falls through to the unsigned return, so a client-set plain value is accepted as if it were signed.
A timedelta max_age is converted with .seconds, which drops the days, so a cookie set for whole days expires at once.

decoys.why: http_date() accepts a datetime, a date or a timestamp and parse_date() turns its output back into a UNIX time, so every form of expires becomes a timestamp.
The padding is stripped to keep = out of the cookie value and restored before decoding in _cookie_verify().

ceiling.summary: _lscmp() now uses hmac.compare_digest(), which raises TypeError for a str with non-ASCII characters; the signature part of a cookie is client-controlled (a quoted cookie may carry octal escapes such as \351), so a crafted cookie makes get_cookie() raise instead of returning the default.
